text:
maria: Anyone seen this? Importing the Redwood SDK in Next.js middleware (edge) throws at runtime even though build succeeds. Error:
```
Uncaught TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier "@redwood/inference-js" - default export not found
```
It's fine in pages/api server handlers.

kevin: Are you bundling? Next Edge runtime disallows CJS default interop and Node builtins. Which entrypoint are you importing?

maria: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'` from /middleware.ts. Build succeeds, runtime error on edge only.

sam: Try `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'` or `import { createClient }` depending on named exports. Also check package.json "exports"  Next needs pure ESM for edge.

emma: We hit something similar with auth token refresh. Workaround there was to ship an explicit edge bundle: `@redwood/inference-js/edge` (points to dist/edge/index.mjs).

kevin: We should add an `edge` export in package.json and remove conditional CJS fallbacks for that path. Also avoid using `node:` prefixed imports in the edge bundle.

maria: Tried dynamic `import()` inside the middleware handler as a last-ditch  still fails at module resolution time.

devrel: :thumbsup: Filed GH issue RW-857: "ESM edge entrypoint and Next middleware compatibility".

tyler: Proposal for package.json exports snippet: "./edge": { "default": "./dist/edge/index.mjs", "types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts" }

emma: I'll add a sample middleware snippet for devex docs showing `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js/edge'` and a minimal middleware example.

kevin: I'll open a PR with the export and add a CI job that runs a small Vercel edge runtime test.

maria: Pushed a minimal repro: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-edge-esm  includes a failing Next 13 middleware example.

devrel: Assigning RW-857 to @kevin and @devrel. ETA: next week. :calendar:

maria: One more gotcha: TypeScript in middleware complains about `Request`/`Response` types unless you add `\"dom\"` to the tsconfig libs for edge.

sam: Good call  we'll add docs: middleware tsconfig should include "dom" lib and recommend `skipLibCheck: true` for smoother DX.
